advances: The actual fiber-volume tables of explicit full-dimensional rational convex bodies can have threshold score \(R(w)/W\sim 3\,2^{-n}\), even when their zero extensions are globally log-concave and every nonempty positive superlevel set has affine dimension \(n\). Consequently there is no absolute \(c>0\) such that \(R(w)\ge cW\) for all such tables. The same bodies have Hellinger gain tending to \(\log 2\), normalized maximal atom tending to zero, and actual maximal mixed-integer depth asymptotic to \(2^{-n}W\). This is an obstruction to the standalone global-threshold inequality. The depth calculation verifies that this family satisfies the locked weak Oertel bound, and the gain does not approach the regime \(G=0\).

proof:
Each ordinary generating rectangle and each special generating segment is the convex hull of finitely many rational points. Hence \(C_m\) is a compact rational polytope. It contains the origin, the \(m\) points \((\mathbf e_r,0,0)\), the point \((\mathbf0,1,0)\), and the point \((\mathbf0,0,N_0^{-1})\). The last two points lie in the ordinary rectangle at \(\mathbf b_0=\mathbf0\), since \(N_0=3^m\ge9\). The differences of these \(m+2\) nonzero points from the origin span \(\mathbb R^{m+2}=\mathbb R^{n+d}\). Thus \(C_m\) is full-dimensional and is a convex body.

All outer coordinates of \(C_m\) lie in \([0,1]^m\). Therefore an integer outer coordinate \(\mathbf x\) of a point in \(C_m\) is Boolean. Fix such a Boolean vector \(\mathbf b\) and express any point of \(C_m\) with outer coordinate \(\mathbf b\) as a convex combination of generating points. If \(b_r=0\), all positively weighted generating points have outer coordinate zero in position \(r\); if \(b_r=1\), all have outer coordinate one there. Applying this to every \(r\) forces every positively weighted point to have outer coordinate \(\mathbf b\). Exactly one prescribed rectangle or segment has this outer coordinate, and that set is convex. Consequently the entire slice of \(C_m\) at \(\mathbf b\) is exactly that prescribed set. Taking integer \(s\) in this slice proves the stated fiber census and excludes all additional integer fibers.

We verify the claim about the actual extension also at noninteger base points. Every generating set contains \((z,0)\) whenever it contains a point with base coordinate \(z\). Thus, by taking convex combinations, \((z,0)\in C_m\) for every \(z\in P_m\). Also, every generating set has height at least \(N_{L-1}^{-1}>0\). A convex combination representing a point \(z\in P_m\) can therefore be lifted with continuous coordinate identically \(N_{L-1}^{-1}\), giving \((z,N_{L-1}^{-1})\in C_m\). Since \(C_m\) is compact and all its continuous coordinates lie in \([0,N_0^{-1}]\), its fiber at \(z\in P_m\) is an interval \([0,f_m(z)]\) with \(N_{L-1}^{-1}\le f_m(z)\le N_0^{-1}\).

For \(z,z'\in P_m\) and \(0<\theta<1\), convexity applied to their upper endpoints gives

\[
\begin{aligned}
f_m((1-\theta)z+\theta z')
&\ge(1-\theta)f_m(z)+\theta f_m(z')\\
&\ge f_m(z)^{1-\theta}f_m(z')^\theta.
\end{aligned}
\]

The first inequality proves concavity on \(P_m\), and the second is the weighted arithmetic-geometric mean inequality. If either base point lies outside \(P_m\), the right-hand side of the log-concavity inequality is zero and the inequality follows from nonnegativity. The endpoint cases \(\theta=0,1\) are identities. This proves global log-concavity of the actual function, including its zero values outside the projection.

The census gives \(N_i\) fibers of weight \(N_i^{-1}\) in each ordinary block, so each such block has total mixed measure one. Each special block has one fiber of weight \(N_0^{-1}\). Hence \(W_m=L+m/N_0\), and the largest weight is \(M_m=N_0^{-1}\).

The positive atom values are exactly \(N_i^{-1}\), \(0\le i<L\). For any \(t>0\) with a nonempty superlevel set, let \(N_i^{-1}\) be the smallest positive atom value at least \(t\). Raising the threshold from \(t\) to \(N_i^{-1}\) leaves the superlevel set unchanged and weakly increases the threshold score. Thresholds with empty superlevel set have score zero. Thus the maximum defining \(R\) is attained at one of these positive atom values. At \(t=N_i^{-1}\), precisely the ordinary blocks indexed by \(0,\ldots,i\), together with all \(m\) special fibers, occur. The geometric series gives

\[
\begin{aligned}
N_i^{-1}|E_m(N_i^{-1})|
&=\frac{m+\sum_{h=0}^iN_h}{N_i}\\
&=\frac{m}{N_0}3^{-i}+\frac{3^{i+1}-1}{2\cdot3^i}\\
&=\frac32-\left(\frac12-\frac{m}{N_0}\right)3^{-i}.
\end{aligned}
\]

The binomial theorem gives \(3^m=(1+2)^m>2m\), so \(m/N_0<1/2\). The displayed score therefore increases strictly with \(i\). Its maximum at \(i=L-1\) is exactly the asserted formula, and it is strictly less than \(3/2\).

Every nonempty positive superlevel set contains all points with maximum weight. In particular, it contains \((\mathbf0,0)\), \((\mathbf0,1)\), and \((\mathbf e_r,0)\) for \(1\le r\le m\). The differences of the latter \(m+1\) points from \((\mathbf0,0)\) are the coordinate basis of \(\mathbb R^{m+1}\). These points are affinely independent, proving \(\dim\operatorname{aff}E_m(t)=n\) for every \(t>0\) with \(E_m(t)\ne\varnothing\).

Next consider every integer reflection center \(j=(\mathbf a,k)\in\mathbb Z^m\times\mathbb Z\). A nonzero summand in \(H^{(m)}_j\) has two positive-weight endpoints, whose outer coordinates lie in \(\{0,1\}^m\). Their sum is \(2\mathbf a\). Coordinatewise, the sum of two Boolean coordinates can be even only when those coordinates are equal. Therefore both outer endpoints equal \(\mathbf a\), this vector is Boolean, and the outer component of the displacement \(v\) is zero. There are no reflected pairs between different outer blocks at any integer center.

If \(\mathbf a=\mathbf b_i\), positive endpoint pairs require \(0\le k\le N_i-1\); otherwise \(H^{(m)}_j=0\). For an integer \(k\) in this interval, the remaining displacement \(u\in\mathbb Z\) must satisfy \(|u|\le\min(k,N_i-1-k)\). Every such summand equals \(N_i^{-1}\), and hence \(H^{(m)}_{(\mathbf b_i,k)}=(1+2\min(k,N_i-1-k))/N_i\). This is at most one, with equality exactly when \(k=(N_i-1)/2\), an integer because \(N_i\) is odd. In a special outer block, the only positive reflection sum is \(H^{(m)}_{(\mathbf e_r,0)}=N_0^{-1}<1\). At every remaining integer center the sum is zero. This exhausts all integer centers and proves \(H_{*,m}=1\), attained exactly at the central integer points of the ordinary blocks. Since \(2^n=2B\), the definitions now give \(G_m=\log(2B/W_m)\) and \(\rho_m=2B/(N_0W_m)\).

For the lower depth bound, \(p_m=(\mathbf0,(N_0-1)/2,1/(2N_0))\) belongs to \(S_m\). The mixed set in the ordinary block at \(\mathbf0\) is \(\{\mathbf0\}\times\{0,\ldots,N_0-1\}\times[0,N_0^{-1}]\), and its mixed measure is one. Reflection about \(p_m\) sends \((\mathbf0,k,y)\) to \((\mathbf0,N_0-1-k,N_0^{-1}-y)\). It preserves this set and its mixed measure, since it permutes the integer \(k\) and preserves the length of each fiber.

Fix any closed ambient halfspace \(H\) containing \(p_m\). For any point \(q\) in this ordinary block, at least one of \(q\) and \(2p_m-q\) lies in \(H\). Indeed, if a proper halfspace is written \(H=\{q:a\cdot q\ge b\}\), both points being outside would imply \(2a\cdot p_m<2b\), contrary to \(p_m\in H\). Integrating this pointwise assertion over the block and using reflection invariance gives twice the mixed measure of its intersection with \(H\) at least one. The whole-space case, if admitted among halfspaces, is immediate. Thus \(\mu_m(H)\ge1/2\) for every such \(H\), including those with positive mixed measure on their boundary. It follows that \(h_{S_m}(p_m)\ge1/2\).

For the upper bound, take an arbitrary \(p=(\mathbf b,s,y)\in S_m\). By the census, \(\mathbf b\) belongs to one of the prescribed outer blocks. Write \(a_{\mathbf b}=N_i^{-1}\) in an ordinary block \(\mathbf b=\mathbf b_i\), and \(a_{\mathbf b}=N_0^{-1}\) in a special block. We have \(0\le y\le a_{\mathbf b}\le M_m\). Choose \(\sigma=1\) if \(y\ge a_{\mathbf b}/2\), and \(\sigma=-1\) otherwise. On an interval \([0,a_{\mathbf b}]\), the condition \(\sigma(y'-y)\ge0\) retains length \(\min(y,a_{\mathbf b}-y)\le a_{\mathbf b}/2\).

Define \(\ell_{\mathbf b}(\mathbf x):=\sum_{r=1}^m(2b_r-1)(x_r-b_r)\). For Boolean \(\mathbf x\), this equals the negative of the number of coordinates in which \(\mathbf x\) differs from \(\mathbf b\). In particular, \(\ell_{\mathbf b}(\mathbf b)=0\), while \(\ell_{\mathbf b}(\mathbf x)\le-1\) at every other Boolean vector. Consider the closed ambient halfspace

\[
H_p:=\{(\mathbf x,s',y'):
\sigma(y'-y)+2M_m\ell_{\mathbf b}(\mathbf x)\ge0\}.
\]

It is proper because its coefficient of \(y'\) is \(\sigma\ne0\), and it contains \(p\) on its boundary. Every point of \(C_m\) has \(0\le y'\le M_m\). At any other integer outer block, therefore, \(\sigma(y'-y)+2M_m\ell_{\mathbf b}(\mathbf x)\le M_m-2M_m=-M_m<0\). Thus \(H_p\) excludes all other mixed-integer outer blocks. In the block at \(\mathbf b\), its defining condition reduces exactly to \(\sigma(y'-y)\ge0\), independently of \(s'\). If the block is ordinary, its \(N_i\) fibers each contribute at most \(N_i^{-1}/2\), giving \(\mu_m(H_p)\le1/2\). If it is special, its only fiber contributes at most \(N_0^{-1}/2<1/2\). Hence \(h_{S_m}(p)\le1/2\) for every \(p\in S_m\). Together with the lower bound at \(p_m\), this proves \(h_{\max}(C_m)=h_{S_m}(p_m)=1/2\), with the required order of the point and halfspace quantifiers.

Finally, \(W_m/B=1-m/2^m+m/(3^m2^m)\to1\), while \(L=2^m-m\to\infty\) and \(N_0=3^m\to\infty\). Since \(0<1/2-m/N_0<1/2\), the exact threshold formula gives \(R(w^{(m)})\to3/2\). It follows that \((R(w^{(m)})/W_m)/(3\,2^{-n})=2BR(w^{(m)})/(3W_m)\to1\). The remaining exact identities imply \(G_m\to\log2\), \(\rho_m\to0\), and \(h_{\max}(C_m)/(2^{-n}W_m)=B/W_m\to1\). For every \(m\ge2\), \(W_m=B-m(1-N_0^{-1})<B\), proving the asserted strict inequality \(B/W_m>1\).

In particular, \(R(w^{(m)})/W_m\to0\), which disproves any dimension-independent positive lower bound for this ratio even under all the proved extension and superlevel-rank properties. The exact depth ratio greater than one shows that every member of this family satisfies the locked inequality for every \(c_0\in(0,1/e)\). The limit \(G_m=\log2+o(1)\) also prevents this sequence from refuting a heavy-atom assertion whose hypothesis is \(G\to0\).
statement:
For every integer \(m\ge2\), put \(B:=2^m\), \(n:=m+1\), \(d:=1\), \(L:=B-m\), and \(N_i:=3^{m+i}\) for \(0\le i<L\). Let \(\mathbf e_1,\ldots,\mathbf e_m\) be the standard unit vectors in \(\mathbb R^m\), and enumerate \(\{0,1\}^m\setminus\{\mathbf e_1,\ldots,\mathbf e_m\}\) as \(\{\mathbf b_0=\mathbf0,\mathbf b_1,\ldots,\mathbf b_{L-1}\}\). Use integer coordinates \(z=(\mathbf x,s)\in\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R=\mathbb R^n\) and continuous coordinate \(y\in\mathbb R\). Define

\[
\begin{aligned}
C_m:=\operatorname{conv}\Bigg(&
\bigcup_{i=0}^{L-1}
\{\mathbf b_i\}\times[0,N_i-1]\times[0,N_i^{-1}]\\
&\quad\cup\bigcup_{r=1}^{m}
\{\mathbf e_r\}\times\{0\}\times[0,N_0^{-1}]
\Bigg).
\end{aligned}
\]

For every real \(z\in\mathbb R^n\), let \((C_m)_z:=\{y:(z,y)\in C_m\}\) and \(f_m(z):=\operatorname{vol}_1((C_m)_z)\), with value zero for an empty fiber. For integer \(z\), write \(w^{(m)}_z:=f_m(z)\), \(W_m:=\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z^n}w^{(m)}_z\), and \(M_m:=\max_{z\in\mathbb Z^n}w^{(m)}_z\). Thus these are actual fiber volumes in the normalization of the locked problem.

For \(t>0\), set \(E_m(t):=\{z\in\mathbb Z^n:w^{(m)}_z\ge t\}\) and \(R(w^{(m)}):=\max_{t>0}t|E_m(t)|\). For every integer reflection center \(j\in\mathbb Z^n\), define \(H^{(m)}_j:=\sum_{v\in\mathbb Z^n}\sqrt{w^{(m)}_{j-v}w^{(m)}_{j+v}}\), and put \(H_{*,m}:=\max_{j\in\mathbb Z^n}H^{(m)}_j\), \(G_m:=\log(2^nH_{*,m}/W_m)\), and \(\rho_m:=2^nM_m/W_m\), using natural logarithms.

Let \(S_m:=C_m\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R)\) and \(\mu_m(A):=\mathcal H_1(S_m\cap A)\). For \(p\in S_m\), define \(h_{S_m}(p):=\inf_{H\ni p}\mu_m(H)\), where \(H\) ranges over closed ambient halfspaces, and put \(h_{\max}(C_m):=\sup_{p\in S_m}h_{S_m}(p)\).

Then \(C_m\) is a full-dimensional rational convex body. If \(P_m\subset\mathbb R^n\) is its projection onto the integer-coordinate space, every fiber over \(P_m\) is \([0,f_m(z)]\), and \(f_m\) is strictly positive and concave on \(P_m\). Its value-zero extension to all of \(\mathbb R^n\), which is already the actual fiber-volume function defined above, is globally log-concave.

The integer fibers have the exact census

\[
w^{(m)}_{(\mathbf x,s)}=
\begin{cases}
N_i^{-1},&\mathbf x=\mathbf b_i,\quad s\in\{0,\ldots,N_i-1\},\quad 0\le i<L,\\
N_0^{-1},&\mathbf x\in\{\mathbf e_1,\ldots,\mathbf e_m\},\quad s=0,\\
0,&\text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\qquad (\mathbf x,s)\in\mathbb Z^m\times\mathbb Z.
\]

Every \(E_m(t)\ne\varnothing\) with \(t>0\) has affine dimension \(n\). Moreover,

\[
\begin{aligned}
W_m&=L+\frac{m}{N_0},
& M_m&=\frac1{N_0},\\
R(w^{(m)})
&=\frac32-\left(\frac12-\frac{m}{N_0}\right)3^{-(L-1)}<\frac32,
& H_{*,m}&=1,\\
G_m&=\log\frac{2B}{W_m},
&\rho_m&=\frac{2B}{N_0W_m},\\
h_{\max}(C_m)&=\frac12,
&\frac{h_{\max}(C_m)}{2^{-n}W_m}&=\frac{B}{W_m}>1.
\end{aligned}
\]

The depth supremum is attained at \(p_m=(\mathbf0,(N_0-1)/2,1/(2N_0))\). As \(m\to\infty\), these identities give

\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{R(w^{(m)})}{W_m}&\sim3\,2^{-n},
&G_m&\longrightarrow\log2,\\
\rho_m&\longrightarrow0,
&\frac{h_{\max}(C_m)}{2^{-n}W_m}&\longrightarrow1.
\end{aligned}
\]
